claimLedger.claim: Leaky bladder may need pelvic floor exercises; ask GP or health visitor any time; postnatal check around 6–8 weeks is a good time to raise problems.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NHS · Your post-pregnancy body · not stated on fetch
claimLedger.limitations: UK maternity pathway timing; Indian postnatal visit schedules differ.

claimLedger.claim: Discuss pelvic floor dysfunction at each postnatal contact; ask recently delivered women about symptoms; list labour-related risk factors; offer ≥3 months supervised PFMT for stress/mixed UI.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NICE · NG210 Pelvic floor dysfunction — Recommendations · Published 9 December 2021
claimLedger.limitations: UK service roles; local Indian staffing models vary.

claimLedger.claim: Offer ≥3 months supervised PFMT as first-line for stress or mixed UI after digital confirmation of contraction.
claimLedger.sourceSection: NICE · NG123 Urinary incontinence and pelvic organ prolapse in women: management — Recommendations · not stated on Recommendations chapter fetch

claimLedger.claim: See a GP for any type of incontinence; diary of fluids and urination may be suggested; pregnancy and vaginal birth listed among risk factors.
